why: No existing kind lets a student draw arrows between two sets. product_builder taps pairs but does not model the diagram, and pair_plotter takes only one point. The new kind would diagnose adding instead of multiplying the count (too few arrows) and omitting the equal pairs such as (3, 3) in X×X. Both are the misconceptions listed for this objective.

product_builder only builds the full product X×Y, and a function is a subset of it. pair_plotter takes a single point. Neither lets the student build a relation and test the 'each element of X appears exactly once' property, so using them would be a forced fit. This objective's misconception list is also empty, so no diagnostic could be attached to an existing kind.

No existing kind lets the student build a relation as a set of ordered pairs or arrows. pair_plotter marks one point only, and product_builder gives the whole product. Neither fits this objective's mathematics, and this objective has no listed misconceptions to map.

pair_plotter takes one lattice point and cannot grade a region or a membership decision. The objective is about deciding membership in X×X, and the open-ended region is not a lattice point. It would diagnose using one bound for both coordinates and confusing the axes with the quadrants. The objective currently lists no misconceptions, so these would need to be authored first.

product_builder grades only the full product X × Y, not a subset chosen by a rule. pair_plotter takes one point at a time and has no rule or arrow diagram. Neither fits writing the relation given by a rule.
product_builder builds X × Y itself, not a subset of it. This objective also has no misconception to map, and a template needs at least one diagnostic, so no honest template is possible.

product_builder allows at most 4 numbers per set, so a 5-element X is out of range. It also grades the whole product, not a rule-chosen subset. pair_plotter grades single points on −5..5 and cannot collect a set of pairs.

number_line_marker works only on a numeric line and its targets are real numbers. Here the range is a subset of an arbitrary finite set Y, read off a diagram. A set-selection widget over labelled diagram elements is needed, and no existing kind provides it. This objective also has no listed misconceptions.

No existing kind plots points from a table onto a curve. pair_plotter takes only one point, and line_drawer only draws straight lines. curve_sketcher is named in the spec fields but not in the contract given here, so its predicates are unknown.
pair_plotter could place the vertex, but it cannot show the opening direction, the axis or the extreme value, so using it would be a forced fit.
area_model only handles expanding or factoring a product of two binomials, not classifying polynomials or finding a degree. Anything else would be an answer box in disguise.

gaps.description: Two columns of dots for X and Y (or X and X). The student draws arrows from elements of X to elements of Y to build the arrow diagram of X×Y or X×X, then plots the same pairs on a Cartesian grid. A live counter shows the number of arrows against n(X)·n(Y).
gaps.why: No existing kind lets a student draw arrows between two sets. product_builder taps pairs but does not model the diagram, and pair_plotter takes only one point. The new kind would diagnose adding instead of multiplying the count (too few arrows) and omitting the equal pairs such as (3, 3) in X×X. Both are the misconceptions listed for this objective.

gaps.description: The student shades or taps the region of the plane that is X×X for an interval X, such as [-2, 3], and classifies points by quadrant or axis. A point given in the stem is dragged into the correct quadrant or onto the correct axis.
gaps.why: pair_plotter takes one lattice point and cannot grade a region or a membership decision. The objective is about deciding membership in X×X, and the open-ended region is not a lattice point. It would diagnose using one bound for both coordinates and confusing the axes with the quadrants. The objective currently lists no misconceptions, so these would need to be authored first.

gaps.description: The student sees X and Y and a rule such as b = 2a + 4. They tap the pairs of X × Y that satisfy the rule, or draw arrows from members of X to members of Y. The relation builds live as an arrow diagram and a cartesian grid together. Errors it would diagnose: arrows reversed, a pair left out, a pair that does not satisfy the rule, and a rule evaluated with a sign error such as 2(-1)+4 taken as 6.
gaps.why: product_builder grades only the full product X × Y, not a subset chosen by a rule. pair_plotter takes one point at a time and has no rule or arrow diagram. Neither fits writing the relation given by a rule.

gaps.description: The student is given a candidate set of pairs and X × Y laid out as a grid. They mark which pairs belong to the relation and see whether the relation is contained in X × Y. They can also add a stray pair from outside X × Y and see that it breaks the subset property. Errors it would diagnose: a relation with pairs outside X × Y, and the idea that a relation must equal X × Y.
gaps.why: product_builder builds X × Y itself, not a subset of it. This objective also has no misconception to map, and a template needs at least one diagnostic, so no honest template is possible.

gaps.need_kind: relation_selector (relation on one set, arrow and cartesian diagram)
gaps.description: The student gets X = {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2} and a rule such as 'a is the additive inverse of b'. They tap the pairs of X × X, or draw arrows from X back to X, and both diagrams update together. This would diagnose a missing (0, 0), a half-built symmetric set, and reversed pairs.
gaps.why: product_builder allows at most 4 numbers per set, so a 5-element X is out of range. It also grades the whole product, not a rule-chosen subset. pair_plotter grades single points on −5..5 and cannot collect a set of pairs.

gaps.description: Two columns of dots, X and Y, are shown. The student drags arrows from elements of X to elements of Y to build a relation that is a function from X to Y, or one that is not, as the stem asks. Any construction with the property is accepted. Live feedback would list the ordered pairs and mark each element of X by its number of arrows. Diagnostics: an element of X with no arrow (not defined on all of X), an element with two or more arrows (one input with several images), or the arrows reversed from Y to X.
gaps.why: product_builder only builds the full product X×Y, and a function is a subset of it. pair_plotter takes a single point. Neither lets the student build a relation and test the 'each element of X appears exactly once' property, so using them would be a forced fit. This objective's misconception list is also empty, so no diagnostic could be attached to an existing kind.

gaps.description: This is the same instrument as for lo:u1-3-1, used for the anchor question. The stem gives X={2,3,4} and Y={2,...,8}, and the relation a = ½b. The student draws the arrows, and the ordered pairs (2,4), (3,6), (4,8) appear live. A second mode would plot the pairs on a cartesian grid and ask which diagram shows a function, using the vertical-line idea. Errors to diagnose: the relation read in the wrong direction (b = ½a), the relation taken as a function without checking that each element of X is used, and arrows drawn from Y to X.
gaps.why: No existing kind lets the student build a relation as a set of ordered pairs or arrows. pair_plotter marks one point only, and product_builder gives the whole product. Neither fits this objective's mathematics, and this objective has no listed misconceptions to map.

gaps.description: A function is shown as an arrow diagram. The student taps the elements of Y that make up the range, and the codomain is shown as the whole of Y. It is graded as a set, like number_line_marker in points mode but on discrete labelled elements. Errors to diagnose: range taken as the whole codomain, range missing an image, and range including elements that no arrow reaches. The student would also tap the domain.
gaps.why: number_line_marker works only on a numeric line and its targets are real numbers. Here the range is a subset of an arbitrary finite set Y, read off a diagram. A set-selection widget over labelled diagram elements is needed, and no existing kind provides it. This objective also has no listed misconceptions.

gaps.description: The student fills in or plots the points of a table of values over a given interval for a quadratic, then sees them joined into a smooth parabola. The widget would diagnose joining points with straight segments, plotting x² as 2x, sign errors for negative x (e.g. (-2)² = -4), and omitting points that show the symmetry.
gaps.why: No existing kind plots points from a table onto a curve. pair_plotter takes only one point, and line_drawer only draws straight lines. curve_sketcher is named in the spec fields but not in the contract given here, so its predicates are unknown.

gaps.description: The student drags a vertex and sets the opening direction, or drags the curve, to match a given quadratic. The widget would show the axis x = -b/2a and the min or max value live. It would diagnose using x = b/2a (sign flip), reading the constant c as the vertex height, confusing a minimum with a maximum when a<0, and reporting the x-coordinate as the extreme value.
gaps.why: pair_plotter could place the vertex, but it cannot show the opening direction, the axis or the extreme value, so using it would be a forced fit.

gaps.description: The student expands or cancels a rule such as x(x-2x²) step by step and then picks the highest surviving power. The widget would diagnose reading the degree from the unsimplified form (mc:u1-4-1:degree-from-unexpanded-form).
gaps.why: area_model only handles expanding or factoring a product of two binomials, not classifying polynomials or finding a degree. Anything else would be an answer box in disguise.
